```tsx
export const StepsDisplay = ({ field, value, props }: FieldWidgetProps<string, { last?: string }>) => {
  const steps = (field.enumValues ?? []).filter((step) => step !== 'cancelled' || value === 'cancelled')
  const at = value === null ? -1 : steps.indexOf(value)
  return (
    <span className="inline-flex items-center gap-1.5">
      {steps.map((step, index) => (
        <span key={step} className={index <= at ? 'size-2 rounded-full bg-primary' : 'size-2 rounded-full bg-border-strong'} />
      ))}
      <span className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">
        {value === null ? '—' : label(value)}
        {props.last === value ? ' ✓' : ''}
      </span>
    </span>
  )
}
```

`field.enumValues` are the steps, in the order the data config lists them, so the same field type works for any enum. `value` is `null` for an empty field. `props.last` is whatever the view says it is; here, the step that ends an order.

### 2. Edit it

An editor gets the same props, and `onChange` to set a new value, and `invalid` when the value it holds is refused:

```tsx
// components/order-steps.tsx
import type { FieldWidgetEditorProps } from '@protobase/ui'

/** The steps as buttons: the current one marked, a click moves to another. */
export const StepsEditor = ({ field, value, onChange }: FieldWidgetEditorProps<string>) => (
  <div role="radiogroup" aria-label={field.name} className="flex flex-wrap gap-1">
    {(field.enumValues ?? []).map((step) => (
      <button
        key={step}
        type="button"
        role="radio"
        aria-checked={step === value}
        onClick={() => onChange(step)}
        className={step === value ? 'rounded-md border border-primary bg-primary-soft px-2 py-1 text-xs text-primary-text' : 'rounded-md border border-border px-2 py-1 text-xs hover:bg-muted'}
      >
        {label(step)}
      </button>
    ))}
  </div>
)
```

`onChange` changes the record on the page, as typing in an input does: the page shows "Unsaved changes", and Save sends it, with the page's checks and conflict handling. A field type has no save of its own.

### 3. Register it

`protobase.ui.tsx` registers the field type under a name, with the storage types it shows:

```tsx
// protobase.ui.tsx
import { definePlugin } from '@protobase/ui'
import { StepsDisplay, StepsEditor } from './components/order-steps'

export { OrdersPerDay } from './components/orders-per-day'

export default definePlugin({
  actions: { send },
  fields: { steps: { of: ['enum'], display: StepsDisplay, editor: StepsEditor } },
})
```

`of: ['enum']` says it shows enum fields. A table cell draws `display` too, unless the field type gives a `cell` of its own, for instance a more compact one.

### 4. Pick it in the view

The view chooses the field type for a field, with props:

```ts
// config/orders/ui.ts
.fields((r) => ({
  status: r.status.help('Where the order is in its life.').widget('steps', { last: 'delivered' }),
}))
```

Run `bun run protobase dev` and open the orders. The status column shows the dots, and so does every place that shows an order's status: its page when it may not be changed, the summary in its sidebar, cards and page elements. On an order you may change, the status is a row of buttons; click one and save.

### 5. What the app checks

A field type shows the storage types it names, and nothing else. Pick it for a text field by mistake, say the order's number:

```ts
number: r.number.widget('steps'),
```

`protobase build` reads which storage types each field type of the bundle shows, and the server refuses to start:

```
error: The views do not match the resources:
  - View "orders": field "number" is text, and its field type "steps" shows only enum
```

In `protobase dev`, the app checks the same as it draws, and shows the number as it would without a field type.

A field type that throws while drawing takes only its own field with it: the field shows as it would without the field type, and the rest of the page draws. So does every field of a field type whose plugin is off.

### 6. One field type for many apps

The `steps` field type above is the project's own, built with its bundle. To give it to other apps too, move `components/order-steps.tsx` into a [plugin](https://docs.protobase.net/guides/first-plugin/) of its own and register it there:

```tsx
// workshop-tools/protobase.ui.tsx
import { definePlugin } from '@protobase/ui'
import { StepsDisplay, StepsEditor } from './components/steps'

export default definePlugin({ name: 'workshop-tools', fields: { steps: { of: ['enum'], display: StepsDisplay, editor: StepsEditor } } })
```

Each app lists the plugin and picks `.widget('steps')` in its views. The app checks the storage types when it draws; the server checks only the field types of the bundle's own plugins, since it never loads remote code.

## A custom record card

Draw each card of a cards display with a component of your own, and keep the built-in card as its fallback.

A list can show its records as [cards](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/ui-config/#list-displays) beside its table: a title, a subtitle, a badge and a few small fields. Rijnland's sales team wants order cards that lead with the total and the customer, the way they talk about orders. That is a card component: the list page still loads the orders, filters, sorts and links each card to its order; the component only draws what is inside a card. This guide adds one to the ERP example (`examples/erp`).

### 1. The card

A card component gets `row`, one record of the list:

```tsx
// components/order-card.tsx
import type { RecordCardProps } from '@protobase/ui'

/** An order as a card: its number and total, the customer, and its status. */
export const OrderCard = ({ row }: RecordCardProps) => (
  <span className="flex flex-col gap-1">
    <span className="flex items-baseline justify-between gap-2">
      <span className="font-mono text-xs text-muted-foreground">{String(row.record.number)}</span>
      <span className="font-semibold tabular-nums">€{Number(row.record.total).toFixed(2)}</span>
    </span>
    <span className="truncate font-medium">{row.labels.company_id ?? String(row.record.company_id)}</span>
    <span className="mt-1 self-start rounded-md bg-primary-soft px-1.5 py-0.5 text-xs text-primary-text">{String(row.record.status)}</span>
  </span>
)
```

`row.record` is the order as the list API gives it, and `row.labels` the name of the record each relation points at: `company_id` is the company's id, `labels.company_id` its name. `row.key` is the order's key.

The whole card is a link to the order, so the component draws no links or buttons of its own; the app draws the card's border, padding and hover, in the app's [theme](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/theme/).

### 2. Export it

```tsx
// protobase.ui.tsx
export { OrderCard } from './components/order-card'
```

### 3. Use it in the view

Declare the component in the view and give it to a cards display. The fields the display names are the fields the cards get, so name every field the card reads:

```ts
// config/orders/ui.ts
import { component } from '@protobase/layout'

export const OrderCard = component('OrderCard')

// ...
.list((r, d) => ({
  columns: [r.number, r.company_id, r.status, r.total, r.created_at],
  sort: [[r.created_at, 'desc']],
  displays: [d.cards({ title: r.number, subtitle: r.company_id, badge: r.status, meta: [r.total] }, { card: OrderCard })],
}))
```

Run `bun run protobase dev`, open the orders and switch to Cards: each order is drawn by `OrderCard`. The display keeps everything else the list has: its search, filters, sort menu, the count of orders and loading more as you scroll.

`protobase build` fails when the config declares `OrderCard` and `protobase.ui.tsx` does not export it. A card from a [plugin](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/plugins/) is declared with the plugin's name, `component('OrderCard', { plugin: 'sales-tools' })`.

### 4. When the card fails

The fields in `d.cards` do double duty: they are also the built-in card, `title` over `subtitle` with `badge` and the `meta` fields. Each card falls back to it:

- when the component throws while drawing, that card alone;
- when no component is registered under the name, for instance because its plugin is off, every card.

So a broken card still shows each order's number, customer and status, and still opens it.

## Moving onto the plugin build

What changes for a project whose protobase.ui.tsx was built into the admin app, now that protobase build makes it a plugin beside a prebuilt app.

Until 0.12, `protobase build` built the whole admin app into each bundle, with the project's `protobase.ui.tsx` and every `--extend` folder's compiled into it. Each bundle was frozen at the `@protobase/ui` it was built with: the app's fixes reached it only with a rebuild. From 0.12 the admin app is prebuilt once per release, and `protobase build` builds the project's `protobase.ui.tsx` as a [plugin](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/plugins/) beside it. The project's code is written the same way; this guide moves a project over and says what to look at.

### 1. Update and rebuild

Move the project's `@protobase` packages to 0.12 or newer, as for any release, and build:

```sh
bun add @protobase/cli@^0.12 @protobase/server@^0.12 @protobase/schema@^0.12 @protobase/layout@^0.12 @protobase/ui@^0.12
bun run protobase build
```

```
built dist: protobase.config.js, public/ with plugins app and protobase.bundle.json (api /api)
```

A bundle of an older release is refused by the 0.12 runtime, as every new minor below 1.0 is; this one rebuild is the whole migration for most projects. The new bundle holds:

```
dist/
  protobase.config.js
  public/
    index.html, assets/      the prebuilt admin app
    plugins/app/             protobase.ui.tsx, as the plugin app
    protobase.theme.css      empty until the project has a theme
    protobase.favicon.svg    Protobase's until the project has its own
  protobase.bundle.json      version 3, naming the plugins and the app's version
```

### 2. Check protobase.ui.tsx

Nothing in it has to change: its named component exports, `defineUi({ actions, shell, extends })` and the components it registers work as before. `definePlugin` is the same function under its new name, and also takes [field types](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/plugins/#field-types). Three things a plugin cannot do, which a built-in `protobase.ui.tsx` could, fail the build or show at once:

- **Modules of the shared packages.** `react`, `react/jsx-runtime`, `react-dom` and `@protobase/ui` come from the app, by those names. An import of another module of theirs, such as `react-dom/client` or a file inside `@protobase/ui`, fails the build: import from the package's main entry instead.
- **Browser work at the top level.** The build loads `protobase.ui.tsx` once in Node to read its field types. Code that touches `window`, `document` or `localStorage` when a module loads fails the build; move it into a component, a hook or a handler.
- **A data library of its own.** A component that used `@tanstack/react-query` directly found the app's query client while it was built into the app; as a plugin it carries its own copy, which does not. Read through `@protobase/ui`'s hooks (`useList`, `useRecord`, `useClient`), which share the app's cache and session.

### 3. Check its styles

The project's Tailwind classes are built into the plugin's own stylesheet, `plugins/app/assets/styles-<hash>.css`: utilities only, each reading the app's [tokens](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/theme/). `bg-primary` and `rounded-md` look as before. A class that only worked because the app's own stylesheet happened to have it is now in the plugin's too, so nothing is lost. To change the app's colors, radius or font, write a [`protobase.theme.css`](https://docs.protobase.net/guides/theme-an-app/), not rules against the app's markup.

### 4. Extensions

Each `--extend` folder's `protobase.ui.tsx` becomes a plugin of its own, `plugins/<name>/`, named by its `package.json`, else its folder, and merged before the project's, as before. Its `protobase.config.ts` is merged into the config module as before. Two extensions that would be plugins of one name fail the build: give one's `package.json` another `name`.

### 5. Hosts

A host that serves `public/` as before keeps working: `index.html` for navigations, files for the rest. Two things are new:

- The plugins' `assets/` folders, `public/plugins/<name>/assets/`, are named by their content like `public/assets/`: serve them as immutable too. `plugin.json`, `protobase.theme.css` and `protobase.favicon.svg` are served with `no-cache`.
- A host that keeps the prebuilt app of newer releases may serve it for the manifest's `shell.paths`, so the app gets that release's fixes without a rebuild (see [the shell](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/plugins/#the-shell)). `protobase serve` does so with its own when every plugin of the bundle loads in it.

### 6. protobase dev

Nothing changes: `protobase dev` builds `protobase.ui.tsx` into its page with hot reload, as before, and serves the theme too. `protobase build && protobase serve dist` runs the bundle as a host does, with the project's UI loaded as the plugin `app`.

### After the move

From now on, a release of Protobase within the same minor needs no rebuild of the project's UI: the app it runs in is the release's, and the plugin keeps working within its [plugin API](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/plugins/#versions). The server config still follows the [bundle's rule](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/versioning/#bundles-and-runtimes), so a new minor below 1.0 is still a rebuild.

## Showing another app's records

Two Protobase apps, where the shop's admin app shows the service desk's tickets with its own pages, sidebar and links.

Sam runs a web shop, and its customers' questions land in the company's service desk, a Protobase app of its own. When a customer calls about an order, Sam's people look the order up in the shop's admin app, then open the desk in another tab to find the customer's ticket. They want the tickets in the shop's admin app, next to the orders: a list, each ticket's page, the open ones in the sidebar, and a status they can change. The desk's agents keep working in the desk.

This guide makes the desk's tickets a [remote resource](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/remote-resources/) of the shop: the shop draws them with its own pages, while the desk keeps the data, the rules and the views. Nothing is copied and nothing is proxied: the shop's admin app reads the desk's API with the shop's own sign-in.

### 1. Two apps

You need two Protobase projects, each with its own database, its own [admin store](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/auth/#admin-store) and a user: the from-scratch preset (`examples/scratch` in the repository) is enough for both. Each runs on its own origin; this guide runs them side by side on one machine:

| | `BETTER_AUTH_URL` in its `.env` | Started with |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The service desk | `http://localhost:4720` | `protobase dev --port 4720` |
| The shop | `http://localhost:4710` | `protobase dev --port 4710` |

`BETTER_AUTH_URL` matters here: it is the issuer of each app's tokens, and the desk will recognise the shop's tokens by it.

The shop has its orders. The desk has tickets and their notes:

```ts
// desk: config/tickets/data.ts
import { f, resource } from '@protobase/schema'

type Caller = { user: { roles: string[] } }
const deskOnly = (ctx: unknown) => (ctx as Caller).user.roles.includes('admin')

export const tickets = resource('tickets')
  .table('tickets')
  .fields({
    id: f.integer().readOnly().filterable().sortable(),
    title: f.text().filterable().sortable(),
    customer_email: f.text().filterable(),
    status: f.enum(['open', 'waiting', 'closed']).filterable().sortable(),
    updated_at: f.timestamp().readOnly().filterable().sortable(),
  })
  .primaryKey((r) => r.id)
  .search((r) => [r.title, r.customer_email])
  .access({ delete: deskOnly })

export const ticketNotes = resource('ticket_notes')
  .table('ticket_notes')
  .fields({
    id: f.integer().readOnly().filterable().sortable(),
    ticket_id: f.relation('tickets').filterable(),
    body: f.text(),
    created_at: f.timestamp().readOnly().sortable(),
  })
  .primaryKey((r) => r.id)
  .access({ delete: deskOnly })
```

Only the desk's own admins delete: the [access rule](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/access/) holds for everyone who reaches the desk's API, the shop's people included.

```ts
// desk: config/tickets/ui.ts
import { l, view } from '@protobase/schema'
import type { ticketNotes, tickets } from './data'

const recent = { status: 'status', tones: { open: 'warning', waiting: 'neutral', closed: 'success' }, orderBy: 'updated_at desc' } as const

export const ticketsView = view<typeof tickets>('tickets')
  .title((r) => r.title)
  .names({ singular: 'Ticket', plural: 'Tickets' })
  .nav({ group: 'Support', recent })
  .fields((r) => ({ customer_email: r.customer_email.label('Customer'), status: r.status.format('badge'), updated_at: r.updated_at.label('Changed').format('relative') }))
  .list((r) => ({ columns: [r.title, r.customer_email, r.status, r.updated_at], sort: [[r.updated_at, 'desc']] }))
  .filters((r, w) => [w.facets(r.status)])
  .layout((r) => [
    l.section('Ticket', [r.title, r.customer_email, r.status]),
    l.related('Notes', { resource: 'ticket_notes', field: 'ticket_id', sort: 'created_at desc', columns: ['body', 'created_at'], empty: 'No notes yet.' }),
  ])

export const ticketNotesView = view<typeof ticketNotes>('ticket_notes').nav({ hidden: true })
```

That is the desk's admin app as its agents use it. Nothing in it knows about the shop yet.

### 2. The desk lets the shop's people in

The shop's admin app will call the desk's API from the browser, with the token the shop gave the signed-in person. The desk needs to accept two things: that token, and calls from the shop's origin.

The token: list the shop as a trusted app in the desk's authenticator, and say what the shop's roles are at the desk:

```ts
// desk: auth/auth.ts
export const authenticate = betterAuthAuthenticator({
  auth,
  tenant: 1,
  // The shop's admins sign in at the shop; the desk takes the shop's tokens and calls them `shop` here.
  apps: [{ issuer: 'http://localhost:4710', roles: { admin: 'shop' }, tenant: 1 }],
})
```

The desk now checks a token from the shop against the shop's keys, at `http://localhost:4710/api/auth/jwks`. Its holder is `shop` at the desk, never the desk's `admin`, so the `deskOnly` rule keeps tickets from being deleted from the shop; a shop user with any other role is refused. The [reference](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/remote-resources/#signing-in-at-the-source) has the details, such as the ids those users get.

The origin: the shop's admin app runs on `http://localhost:4710`, so the desk answers [CORS](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/api/#cors) for it:

```ts
// desk: protobase.config.ts
import * as config from './config'
import { auth, authenticate } from './auth/auth'

// The shop's admin app, on its own origin, calls this API from the browser.
export default { config, auth, authenticate, options: { cors: ['http://localhost:4710'] } }
```

`protobase dev` reloads the desk.

### 3. The shop draws the tickets

The shop lists the desk as a source, with the resources it draws from it:

```ts
// shop: protobase.config.ts
import * as config from './config'
import { auth, authenticate } from './auth/auth'

export default {
  config,
  auth,
  authenticate,
  options: {
    sources: [{ url: 'http://localhost:4720/api/v1', label: 'Service desk', resources: ['tickets', 'ticket_notes'] }],
  },
}
```

`url` is the desk's resources API, and `label` its name when the shop's people cannot reach it. The notes are there because a ticket's page lists them: what the shop does not draw, it does not show. A platform that runs the shop can set the same list in `PROTOBASE_SOURCES`, without touching the shop's code:

```sh
PROTOBASE_SOURCES='[{"url":"http://localhost:4720/api/v1","label":"Service desk","resources":["tickets","ticket_notes"]}]'
```

Had the shop a resource or page called `tickets` of its own, it would now refuse to start, naming both: `/tickets` can only be one thing.

### 4. The tickets in the shop

Sign in to the shop. The sidebar has a Support group with Tickets and the desk's recent tickets under it, each with its status; `/tickets` is the desk's list, with its columns, its status filter and its search, and the breadcrumbs read "Support › Tickets":

A ticket opens at `/tickets/1`, with its notes from the desk, and the trail back to the list. Change the status and Save: the shop's admin app writes it to the desk with the ticket's ETag, under the desk's rules, and the ticket moves in the sidebar. The global search in the top bar finds tickets too.

(The stories run on made-up data, with a summary section the next section describes.)

Behind it, the shop's admin app read the desk's `/api/meta` with the shop's token, kept the tickets and notes, and placed them as the desk's view says. Every list and save went straight from the browser to the desk.

### 5. A view for the shop's people

"Support" is how the desk's agents think of tickets. In the shop they are about customers, and only the open ones matter in the sidebar. The desk decides what the shop's people see, so it gives the role it gave them, `shop`, a [view of its own](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/ui-config/#actions-and-views-per-role):

```ts
// desk: config/tickets/ui.ts
// What the shop's people see: the tickets of their customers, next to the shop's orders, and the open ones first.
export const shopTicketsView = ticketsView
  .forRoles(['shop'])
  .names({ singular: 'Customer ticket', plural: 'Customer tickets' })
  .nav({ group: 'Sales', recent: { ...recent, filter: 'status != "closed"' } })
```

After a reload, "Customer tickets" sits in the shop's own Sales group, under Orders, and its recent tickets are the ones still open. The desk's agents still see Support › Tickets.

### 6. When the desk is down

Stop the desk and reload the shop. The orders work as before. The tickets stay in the sidebar, under "Service desk" and marked, and `/tickets` says what is wrong, with a way to try again:

Start the desk again and press **Try again**: the tickets are back. The same happens when the desk answers but does not accept the shop's sign-in, for instance when its `apps` does not list the shop, with the desk's own reason.

### Custom sections

The desk's views can name [custom components](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/custom-components/), such as a timeline of the ticket with `l.custom(TicketTimeline)`. The shop draws them by name from its [plugins](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/plugins/), so the desk ships them as a plugin, built with `protobase build-plugin` and served wherever the shop's browser can load it, and the shop lists it with the source, for instance:

```sh
PROTOBASE_PLUGINS='http://localhost:4720/plugins/desk/plugin.json'
```

Inside, the component reads the ticket with `useLayoutRecord()`, and `useList` and `useRecord` read the desk for the desk's resources. Without the plugin, the shop draws the component's fallback in its place and everything else of the ticket.

### Where to go from here

- [Remote resources](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/remote-resources/): how it works, the contract between an app and its sources, and the API.
- [Your first plugin](https://docs.protobase.net/guides/first-plugin/): build the plugin a source's views need.
- [Access](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/access/): what the role you give another app's users may do.

## Exporting a list

Let users save a list as an Excel or CSV file, limit how many rows a file holds, or take Export off a list.

Every list in the admin can be saved as a file: Rijnland's finance team wants this month's invoices in Excel, and the warehouse wants a CSV of the stock moves for a supplier. Nothing needs setting up for that; this guide shows what users get, and how a view limits it or takes it away. It uses the ERP example (`examples/erp`).

### 1. Export a list

Run `bun run protobase dev`, open the orders and filter them, by status for instance. **Export** beside the title opens a dialog:

- **Format**: an Excel workbook (`.xlsx`) or a CSV file.
- **Rows**: the orders the list finds, with its filters, search and sort. With orders selected in the table, **Export N** beside **Delete N** opens the same dialog with the selected ones.
- **Values**: **As shown** writes what the list shows, such as "Shipped" and the company's name; **Raw values** writes what is stored, such as `shipped` and the company's key.
- **Columns**: the list's columns, in its order. Tick other fields to add them, and move any column up or down.

The dialog says how many rows that is. **Export** asks where to save the file in Chrome and Edge, which then write it as it is built, and downloads it in other browsers. The browser builds the file while it reads the orders page by page, so a large export costs the server no more than scrolling through the list would; **Cancel** stops it.

### 2. Limit or take it off

A view can limit how many rows one file holds, or take Export off its list:

```ts
// config/orders/ui.ts
export const ordersView = view<typeof orders>('orders')
  // ...
  .export({ maxRows: 50_000 })
```

```ts
// config/stock_moves/ui.ts
export const stockMovesView = view<typeof stockMoves>('stock_moves')
  // ...
  .export(false)
```

With a limit, the dialog says when the list finds more rows than a file holds, and the file holds the first ones in the list's order.

### 3. What a file holds

A file holds what the user could read in the list, and no more: the rows come from the same list API, as that user, so their role's [row filters and field lists](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/access/#capabilities) apply, and a [sensitive field](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/data-config/#sensitive-fields) is never offered. To keep a field out of someone's exports, keep it out of what their role may read. A view's limit only shapes the page; someone who may read the orders can still read them all through the API.

The [UI config](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/ui-config/#exports) has the details: how cells are typed in a workbook, how a CSV file is quoted, and how files are named.

## Importing records from a spreadsheet

Bring a spreadsheet of companies into the admin app with the list's Import, update them from another, and turn Import off where it does not belong.

Rijnland's sales team keeps a spreadsheet of companies they met at a trade fair, and wants them in the ERP example (`examples/erp`) without typing each one. Every list offers **Import** to a user who may create its records, so there is nothing to build: this guide walks through an import, an update from a second file, and turning Import off. The [reference](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/ui-config/#importing-records) has every rule.

### 1. Import new records

Save the spreadsheet as it is (`.xlsx`), or as **CSV UTF-8**. Its first row names the columns:

| Name | City | Country | Status | Email |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Hoogland Fietsen | Leiden | NL | Lead | inkoop@hoogland.test |
| De Spaak | Delft | NL | lead | |

Open **Companies**, press **Import** and choose the file. Each column whose header is a field's label or name is mapped already: Country is the label the companies' view gives `country_code`, a relation whose column holds each country's key. Map other columns, or leave them at **Do not import**. Set **Numbers** and **Dates** to how the file writes them. Fields a new company needs that no column fills are named above **Check rows**, which waits for them.

**Check rows** reads the whole file and writes nothing. It shows the first rows as they will be saved and lists each row with a problem, such as a country no record has or a status that is none of Lead, Active and Dormant (`lead` is fine: case and spacing do not count). Those rows are skipped. An empty Email is saved empty; an empty cell is never filled with a default.

**Import** saves the rows in batches of 100, each batch on its own. A row the server refuses is listed with the server's reason while the rest are saved, and **Cancel import** stops after the batch it is in. The summary counts what was created, updated, skipped and failed; **Download** gives the rows not imported, with their line in the file and why, to fix and import again.

### 2. Update records from a file

A second sheet has the companies' VAT numbers, by name:

| Name | VAT number |
| --- | --- |
| Hoogland Fietsen | NL001234567B01 |

Choose **Update** under **Rows**, then **Find records by** Name and **Found in column** Name. Name is a filterable field, so the import can look the companies up; a name two companies share is a problem on its row rather than a guess. A row whose name finds no company is not imported; **Create or update** would create it instead.

### 3. Turn Import off

When a list's records should never come from a file, such as invoices that only orders should make, turn its Import off in the view:

```ts
// invoices/ui.ts
export const invoicesView = view<typeof invoices>('invoices').import(false)
```

Turning it off removes the button, not a right: the API takes the same writes from any client, and the server checks each one, so a user who may not create a record, or write one of its fields, is refused per row as on the record page.

## A create page of your own

Replace a resource's create form with a page of the app's own, built from the app's form parts, that creates records through an API function.

Pip's bike shop books repairs at the desk, and a booking is more than a row: the workshop wants to know what the bike needs, in words a customer understands, and the shop's API function plans the job. This guide gives the repairs a page of their own for that, opened by **New** on their list, and lets the API refuse plain creates. It uses the bike shop of the [first guide](https://docs.protobase.net/guides/table-to-admin/).

### 1. The page

A create page is a [composed page](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/layouts/) like any other, with a [component](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/custom-components/#components) of the project's own in it:

```tsx
// config/pages/book-repair.tsx
/** @jsxImportSource @protobase/layout */
import { Page, component, page } from '@protobase/layout'

export const BookRepair = component('BookRepair')

export const bookRepair = page(
  'book-repair',
  <Page title="Book a repair" description="What the bike needs, so the workshop can plan it.">
    <BookRepair />
  </Page>,
  { roles: ['desk', 'admin'] },
)
```

Its `roles` say who may book: they are the people who get the page, and so **New**.

### 2. The component

The component asks its questions with the [form parts](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/custom-components/#form-parts) of `@protobase/ui`, so it looks like the app's own forms, and keeps the answers in the address, so a reload keeps them:

```tsx
// components/book-repair.tsx, exported from protobase.ui.tsx: export { BookRepair } from './components/book-repair'
import { Choices, Field, Form, Input, Section, useAppAddress, useClient } from '@protobase/ui'
import { useState } from 'react'

const kinds = [
  { value: 'service', label: 'Service', description: 'The whole bike checked: brakes, gears, tyres and chain.' },
  { value: 'flat', label: 'Flat tyre', description: 'A new inner tube, and the tyre checked for what caused it.' },
  { value: 'other', label: 'Something else', description: 'Say what is wrong at the desk.' },
]

export const BookRepair = () => {
  const { address, go } = useAppAddress()
  const client = useClient()
  const [saving, setSaving] = useState(false)
  const [error, setError] = useState<unknown>()
  const values = address?.kind === 'create' ? (address.values ?? {}) : {}
  const answer = (patch: Record<string, string>) => go({ kind: 'create', resource: 'repairs', values: { ...values, ...patch } }, { replace: true })

  const book = () => {
    setSaving(true)
    client.invoke('book-repair', { body: values }).then(
      (repair) => go({ kind: 'record', resource: 'repairs', key: (repair as { id: number }).id }),
      (failure) => {
        setSaving(false)
        setError(failure)
      },
    )
  }

  return (
    <Form submit="Book repair" disabled={!values.bike || !values.kind} saving={saving} error={error} errorTitle="Not booked" onSubmit={book}>
      <Section title="The bike">
        <div className="flex flex-col gap-5">
          <Field label="Bike" required help="Make and model, as on the frame.">
            <Input aria-label="Bike" value={values.bike ?? ''} onChange={(event) => answer({ bike: event.target.value })} />
          </Field>
          <Field label="What it needs" required>
            <Choices name="kind" label="What it needs" options={kinds} value={values.kind} onChange={(kind) => answer({ kind })} />
          </Field>
        </div>
      </Section>
    </Form>
  )
}
```

Without a `title`, the `Form` sits under the page's heading, with its button after the sections.

### 3. Point the view at it

```ts
// config/repairs/ui.ts
export const repairsView = view<typeof repairs>('repairs')
  // ...
  .create({ page: 'book-repair' })
```

**New** on the repairs list now opens the page at `/repairs/new`, and so does every link to a new repair, such as one on a customer's page with `values: { customer_id: '{id}' }`. Someone the page leaves out gets no **New**, and `/repairs/new` tells them they cannot create repairs; the plain create form no longer shows. The server refuses a page name it does not know when it starts.

### 4. Create through a function

With its own page, the shop can make the [API function](https://docs.protobase.net/guides/api-functions/) `book-repair` the only way in: it checks the answers, plans the job and inserts the repair with `db`, which skips the access rules. The resource's API then refuses creates:

```ts
// config/repairs/data.ts
export const repairs = resource('repairs')
  // ...
  .access({ create: () => false })
```

**New** follows the page, not this rule, so it stays for the desk. **Import** on the list follows the rule, and goes.

The [UI config](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/ui-config/#create-pages) has the details.

## Reference pages

For what the guides leave out, read a reference page: each is Markdown at its URL, so fetch the one you need instead of the HTML page.

- [Data config](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/data-config.md): Resources in data.ts, every field type and option, keys and relations, soft delete, tenants, search, validation and access.
- [UI config](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/ui-config.md): Views in ui.ts, with names, list columns, editing in the list, filters, charts (graphs of records per day or per value), exports to Excel and CSV, record layouts, related records (in a section or as dots in a list column), field hints, actions (with a dialog of inputs when they ask for some) and views per role.
- [Architecture](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/architecture.md): How the packages are laid out, which package may import which, and where tests and stories live.
- [REST API](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/api.md): The REST API that @protobase/server generates, with its routes, access, filters, writes, batches and errors.
- [Files](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/files.md): File fields, uploads with types detected from the content, downloads, derived fields, image variants and placeholders, external URLs, image referrers, and how stored files are deleted.
- [Events](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/events.md): Events a resource declares, and how the database captures every change they are raised from, through the API or not.
- [Webhooks](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/webhooks.md): Subscriptions that deliver resource events to URLs, API functions and code, signed with Standard Webhooks, retried and shaped for who receives them.
- [Jobs](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/jobs.md): Background jobs in the app's own database, enqueued with its writes, retried with backoff, run in order per group, and checked at startup.
- [Email](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/email.md): The SMTP server and sender an app's mail goes out through, and emails of the app's own, written as React components with typed data and sent from jobs, hooks and API functions.
- [Access](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/access.md): Roles, capabilities with field lists and row filters, field rules, anonymous access, and what they default to.
- [Login with Better Auth](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/auth.md): Sign-in with Better Auth, with the admin store, sign-in methods and policy, sign-in providers, staff sign-in, roles, tokens and the public endpoints.
- [Client and live UI](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/client.md): The typed fetch client, the TanStack Query hooks and the admin app that runs on them.
- [Layouts](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/layouts.md): Composed pages from JSX layouts, the element tree they compile to, what they may hold, and how data, conditions, actions and access work in them.
- [Blocks](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/blocks.md): Every built-in layout block, its props and what it does, with examples from the ERP's sales overview.
- [Custom components](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/custom-components.md): React components and action handlers of your own in protobase.ui.tsx, used by name from layouts.
- [Plugins](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/plugins.md): React code the admin app loads when it starts instead of building it in, so it keeps working while Protobase moves on.
- [Remote resources](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/remote-resources.md): Resources another Protobase API serves, drawn in an app with its own list pages, record pages, sidebar and links, at their own addresses.
- [Theme](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/theme.md): protobase.theme.css sets the values of the app's tokens, colors, radius and fonts, for light and dark, and keeps working on every release.
- [Sidebar](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/sidebar.md): How sidebar entries are grouped, and how an entry lists recent records with status dots.
- [User menu](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/user-menu.md): The user menu at the bottom of the sidebar, with the app's own account pages and links.
- [Bottom bar](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/bottom-bar.md): Tabs along the bottom of a phone, as on iOS, for the roles that work from one.
- [Assistant](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/assistant.md): The chat beside the admin, who sees it, and its built-in backend on OpenRouter or another OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
- [CLI](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/cli.md): Every protobase command, from scaffold, doctor, dev, build, build-plugin, build-serve and serve to users, organizations and token.
- [Versioning](https://docs.protobase.net/reference/versioning.md): How Protobase is versioned and released, the commit convention behind it, and which bundles a serve runtime runs.
- [@protobase/schema API](https://docs.protobase.net/api/schema.md): Every export of @protobase/schema, generated from its doc comments.
